Vikram Aggarwal, J. (Oral)
The claimants are in appeal seeking enhancement in compensation awarded to them by the Motor
Accident Claims Tribunal, Jalandhar (hereinafter referred to as, 'the Mact') vide award dated
29.08.2024, on account of death of one Darshan Lal in a motor vehicular accident that occurred on
12.10.2018.

sentences.text: 2.  The facts, as emanating from the paper-book, are that the appellants/claimants, who are the widow, two daughters and two sons of Darshan Lal, instituted a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (for short, 'the MV Act'), seeking compensation of Rs.85,00,000/- on account of death of Darshan Lal in a motor vehicular accident, which took place on 12.10.2018.

3. The case of the appellants/claimants was that Darshan Lal, who was 53 years old at the time of his death, was a skilled worker engaged in 1 of 6 the work of stitching Jerseys and Pullovers at large scale and was running a wholesale business of supplying such items in Ludhiana.
It was stated that he was earning Rs.43,000/- per month.
3.1 On 12.10.2018, he boarded a bus bearing registration No.PB- 08-CB-0511 at Village Jamalpur for Ludhiana.
The driver of the said bus (respondent No.1 in the claim petition) was driving at a very high speed.
Despite the passengers requesting him to drive slowly, he paid no heed.
At about 8:30 am, when the bus reached near PEPSI factory, short of Phillaur Town, the driver attempted to overtake a truck.
However, another truck bearing registration No.PB-10-GW-5998 was parked on the left hand side of the road.
The bus rammed into that stationary truck from behind.

The impact was such that Darshan Lal and two other persons, namely, Krishan Bansal and Arpana Bansal,
sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot.
3.2 The accident was witnessed by Shubham Bansal Usha And Others vs United India Insurance Co. Ltd.

4. Respondents No.1 & 2 denied all averments including the factum of accident as also the ownership of respondent No.2 of the bus in question.
Accordingly, the subsequent owners were impleaded as parties.

4.1 Respondent No. 3, in its separate written statement, raised preliminary objections alleging that respondent No. 1 did not possess a valid driving licence and that the offending bus lacked valid travel documents.
On merits, respondent No. 3 denied the averments in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.
2 of 6

4.2 Respondent No. 5, in its written statement, also raised preliminary objections contending that the petition was not maintainable, that no such accident had occurred, and that the claimants had concealed material facts.
On merits, this respondent admitted that he was the owner of truck No. PB-10-GW-5998, that respondent No. 4 was its driver, and that respondent No. 6 was its insurer.
He denied the remaining averments in the petition and sought its dismissal.

4.3 Respondent No. 6, in its separate written statement, likewise raised preliminary objections alleging that respondent No. 4 did not possess a valid licence and travel documents of the offending truck.
On merits respondent No.6 also denied the averments made in the claim petition.
5. From the pleading of the parties, the following issues were framed:-

"1. Whether Darshan Lal son of Sant Ram died in a motor vehicle accident, which took place on 12.10.2018 caused by respondent no.1 while driving offending Bus bearing registration No.PB-08-CB-0511 and respondent no.4 by wrongly parking Truck bearing registration No.PB-10-GW-5998 and the accident had taken place due to contributory negligence of both the drivers?
OPP 2.
Whether claimants are entitled to receive compensation.
If so its quantum and from whom?
OPP 3.
Whether claimants have no locus standi to file the present claim petition and they have not approached the Court with clean hands?
Whether respondent no.1 driver of offending bus was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
If so its effect?
OPR 3 5.
Whether Bus bearing registration No.PB-08- CB-0511 was being plied without requisite documents and, therefore, respondent no.3 is not liable to pay any compensation?
OPR3 6.
Whether claim petition filed by the claimant is false and frivolous?

7. Whether respondent no.4 driver of Truck bearing registration No.PB-10-GW-5998 was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and said truck was not holding valid and requisite documents and therefore, respondent no.6 is not liable to pay any compensation?
OPR6 8
. Relief."

6. The MACT held that the accident, as a result of which Darshan Lal had lost his life, occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus driver as well as the negligent parking of the truck bearing registration No.No.PB-10-GW-5998.
Accordingly, both the drivers of the bus and the truck were held liable for negligence.
7. As regards quantum, the MACT held that there was no evidence as regards the income of the deceased as Rs.43,000/-, as had been claimed by the claimants.
In the absence of any such evidence or even proof of vocation, income of Darshan Lal was assessed as Rs.10,000/- per month, which as per the MACT, was the income of an unskilled person.
The age was assessed as 54 years.
10% future prospects were added.
Accordingly, the following compensation was granted:-
4 of 6 Sr. No. Heads of Claim Awarded by the MACT 2.

Income Rs.11,000/-
3. Deduction 1/4th i.e. Rs.2750/-
5.

Annual dependency Rs.10,89,000 (8250x12x11)
6. Funeral expenses 18,000/-
7. Loss of estate 18,000/-
8. Loss of consortium 48,000/- each (5) Total Compensation 13,65,000/-
8.
I have heard learned counsel for the appellants.
9. Learned counsel representing the appellants submits that the MACT wrongly assessed the income of the deceased.

He submits that deceased Darshan Lal was a highly skilled person engaged in large-scale stitching work of Jerseys and Pullovers and was running a wholesale business supplying of such goods in Ludhiana.

He submits that the income of Darshan Lal was more than Rs.43,000/-
per month.
However, learned counsel concedes that no evidence to this effect was led except the bald statement of PW1 Usha.
She too admitted in her cross-examination that she had no knowledge either about the vocation or the income of her deceased father.
Under the circumstances, the MACT rightly assessed the income of deceased Darshan Lal as Rs.10,000/- per month by treating him as an unskilled person.
I do not find any illegality in the approach adopted by the MACT.
